-- Every signal as one daily value per (source, signal, geo, UTC day).
-- A value that could not be read is NULL with is_available = false: unavailable, never zero.
with trends as (
    select
        'google_trends' as source,
        'search:' || lower(term) as signal,
        case term_group when 'day_off' then 'day_off_intent' else 'hype' end as signal_family,
        geo,
        interest_date as signal_date,
        case when not is_partial then cast(interest as double) end as signal_value,
        not is_partial as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_trends__interest') }}
),

bluesky as (
    select
        'bluesky' as source,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'posts:day_off_gta' else 'posts:day_off' end as signal,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'day_off_gta' else 'day_off_intent' end as signal_family,
        'WORLD' as geo,
        hit_date as signal_date,
        case when bool_and(is_available) then cast(sum(hits_total) as double) end as signal_value,
        bool_and(is_available) as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_bluesky__daily_hits') }}
    group by gta_filter, hit_date
),

hacker_news as (
    select
        'hacker_news' as source,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'posts:day_off_gta' else 'posts:day_off' end as signal,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'day_off_gta' else 'day_off_intent' end as signal_family,
        'WORLD' as geo,
        hit_date as signal_date,
        case when bool_and(is_available) then cast(sum(hits_total) as double) end as signal_value,
        bool_and(is_available) as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_hn__daily_hits') }}
    group by gta_filter, hit_date
),

wikipedia as (
    select
        'wikipedia' as source,
        'pageviews:' || lower(article) as signal,
        case when article = 'Grand_Theft_Auto_VI' then 'hype' else 'reference' end as signal_family,
        'WORLD' as geo,
        view_date as signal_date,
        cast(views as double) as signal_value,
        true as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_wiki__pageviews') }}
)

select * from trends
union all
select * from bluesky
union all
select * from hacker_news
union all
select * from wikipedia

-- One row per UTC day of the study window and its control year, with its place relative
-- to that year's release Thursday.
with spine as (
    select cast(range as date) as date_day
    from range(date '2025-10-01', date '2027-01-01', interval 1 day)
),

years as (
    select
        date_day,
        case when date_day >= date '2026-01-01' then 2026 else 2025 end as study_year
    from spine
),

anchored as (
    select
        date_day,
        study_year,
        case study_year when 2026 then date '2026-11-19' else date '2025-11-20' end as release_day
    from years
)

select
    date_day,
    study_year,
    release_day,
    cast(date_day - release_day as integer) as days_from_release,
    isodow(date_day) as iso_day_of_week,
    dayname(date_day) as day_name,
    case cast(date_day - release_day as integer)
        when 0 then 'release'
        when -7 then 'baseline'
    end as comparison_role,
    study_year = 2026 and date_day = release_day as is_gta_release_day
from anchored

select
    md5(
        signals.source || '|' || signals.signal || '|' || signals.geo || '|'
        || cast(signals.signal_date as varchar)
    ) as signal_day_key,
    signals.source,
    signals.signal,
    signals.signal_family,
    signals.geo,
    signals.signal_date,
    signals.signal_value,
    signals.is_available,
    dates.study_year,
    dates.days_from_release,
    dates.iso_day_of_week,
    dates.comparison_role
from {{ ref('int_signals__daily') }} as signals
inner join {{ ref('dim_date') }} as dates
    on signals.signal_date = dates.date_day

-- Release Thursday over the Thursday before, per signal and study year.
with pairs as (
    select
        source,
        signal,
        signal_family,
        geo,
        study_year,
        max(signal_value) filter (where comparison_role = 'baseline') as baseline_value,
        max(signal_value) filter (where comparison_role = 'release') as release_value,
        coalesce(bool_or(is_available) filter (where comparison_role = 'baseline'), false)
            as is_baseline_available,
        coalesce(bool_or(is_available) filter (where comparison_role = 'release'), false)
            as is_release_available
    from {{ ref('fct_signal_daily') }}
    where comparison_role is not null
    group by source, signal, signal_family, geo, study_year
)

select
    md5(source || '|' || signal || '|' || geo || '|' || cast(study_year as varchar))
        as thursday_lift_key,
    source,
    signal,
    signal_family,
    geo,
    study_year,
    case study_year when 2026 then date '2026-11-19' else date '2025-11-20' end as release_day,
    baseline_value,
    release_value,
    is_baseline_available,
    is_release_available,
    case
        when is_baseline_available and is_release_available and baseline_value > 0
            then release_value / baseline_value
    end as lift,
    signal_family = 'day_off_intent'
    and source in ('google_trends', 'bluesky', 'reddit')
    and (source <> 'google_trends' or baseline_value >= 5) as is_index_component
from pairs

-- The Day-Off Index: geometric mean of per-source lifts (each source the geometric mean of
-- its own component signals), x 100. 100 is a normal week.
with components as (
    select * from {{ ref('fct_thursday_lift') }}
    where is_index_component
),

by_source as (
    select
        study_year,
        source,
        count(*) as signals_total,
        count(lift) as signals_with_lift,
        case
            when count(lift) = count(*) then exp(avg(ln(greatest(lift, 0.01))))
        end as source_lift
    from components
    group by study_year, source
)

select
    study_year,
    case study_year when 2026 then date '2026-11-19' else date '2025-11-20' end as release_day,
    count(*) as sources_total,
    count(source_lift) as sources_with_lift,
    case
        when count(source_lift) = count(*) then 100 * exp(avg(ln(source_lift)))
    end as day_off_index,
    max(case when source = 'google_trends' then source_lift end) as google_trends_lift,
    max(case when source = 'bluesky' then source_lift end) as bluesky_lift,
    max(case when source = 'reddit' then source_lift end) as reddit_lift
from by_source
group by study_year

-- int_signals__daily: the natural grain behind the surrogate key is unique.
select source, signal, geo, signal_date, count(*) as rows_per_key
from {{ ref('int_signals__daily') }}
group by source, signal, geo, signal_date
having count(*) > 1

-- fct_thursday_lift: the natural grain behind the surrogate key is unique.
select source, signal, geo, study_year, count(*) as rows_per_key
from {{ ref('fct_thursday_lift') }}
group by source, signal, geo, study_year
having count(*) > 1

-- A lift is only computed when both Thursdays were actually read.
select *
from {{ ref('fct_thursday_lift') }}
where lift is not null
  and not (is_baseline_available and is_release_available)

-- Every index component signal of the study year has its 2025 control.
select study.source, study.signal, study.geo
from {{ ref('fct_thursday_lift') }} as study
left join {{ ref('fct_thursday_lift') }} as control
    on study.source = control.source
    and study.signal = control.signal
    and study.geo = control.geo
    and control.study_year = 2025
where study.study_year = 2026
  and study.signal_family = 'day_off_intent'
  and study.source in ('google_trends', 'bluesky', 'reddit')
  and control.signal is null

declarations.description: One row per signal per day: every source's daily value in one shape.

population.rule: Every staged day of every source; Bluesky and Hacker News seeds are summed per day and filter.

source.description: google_trends, bluesky, reddit, hacker_news or wikipedia.

signal.description: What is counted, e.g. search:pto, posts:day_off, posts:day_off_gta, pageviews:grand_theft_auto_vi.

signal_family.description: day_off_intent (people saying or searching they are off), day_off_gta (the same, mentioning GTA), hype (interest in GTA itself), reference.

geo.description: US or WORLD. Only Google Trends has a US slice.

signal_date.description: UTC day (Google's own day for Trends).

signal_value.null_rule: NULL when the value could not be read: unavailable, never zero.
signal_value.description: Counts for posts and pageviews; relative 0-100 interest for Trends. Never add across signals or sources.

is_available.description: False when any part of the day's value failed to load or was partial.

assumptions.chosen: sum hits across seeds per day
assumptions.detail: a post matching two seeds counts twice; the double count is the same on both Thursdays, so the lift is unaffected in expectation
docs/methodology.md: missing is unavailable, never zero
Google flags the latest day isPartial while it fills in

declarations.description: One row per UTC day from 2025-10-01 to 2026-12-31, placed relative to that year's release Thursday.

population.rule: Every calendar day in the spine; 2025 days belong to the control year (anchor Thu 20 Nov 2025), 2026 days to the study (anchor Thu 19 Nov 2026).

days_from_release.description: 0 on the anchor Thursday, -7 on the baseline Thursday.

comparison_role.null_rule: NULL on days that are neither Thursday of the comparison

assumptions.detail: same week of November, one year earlier, both a week before US Thanksgiving week

declarations.description: One row per signal per UTC day inside the study and control windows, with its place relative to release.

population.rule: Signal-days whose date falls in dim_date; days outside the spine are dropped by the inner join.

source.description: google_trends, bluesky, reddit, hacker_news or wikipedia.

signal.description: What is counted, e.g. search:pto, posts:day_off, posts:day_off_gta, pageviews:grand_theft_auto_vi.

signal_family.description: day_off_intent (people saying or searching they are off), day_off_gta (the same, mentioning GTA), hype (interest in GTA itself), reference.

geo.description: US or WORLD. Only Google Trends has a US slice.

signal_date.description: UTC day (Google's own day for Trends).

signal_value.null_rule: NULL when the value could not be read: unavailable, never zero.
signal_value.description: Counts for posts and pageviews; relative 0-100 interest for Trends. Never add across signals or sources.

is_available.description: False when any part of the day's value failed to load or was partial.

comparison_role.null_rule: NULL except on the two compared Thursdays

assumptions.detail: the study compares Thursdays in Oct-Nov 2026 against the same weeks of 2025; the inner join to dim_date keeps only that spine
the key is md5 of the composite Dex drafts as the grain, so the two describe the same rows; MetricFlow needs a single-column primary entity

declarations.description: One row per signal per study year: the release Thursday's value over the Thursday before.

population.rule: Every (source, signal, geo, study year) that has a row on either compared Thursday.

baseline_value.null_rule: NULL when the baseline Thursday is not available

release_value.null_rule: NULL until the release Thursday has closed and loaded

lift.null_rule: NULL unless both Thursdays are available and the baseline is above zero

is_index_component.description: True for the day-off intent signals of Google Trends (baseline >= 5), Bluesky and Reddit.

assumptions.chosen: day_off_intent signals of google_trends, bluesky and reddit
assumptions.detail: Hacker News is too sparse (334 hits in 107 days, .dex/review/05); Wikipedia is hype or reference only

assumptions.chosen: excluded from the index when the baseline is below 5
assumptions.detail: Trends rounds to integers; a baseline of 1-4 turns a one-point wobble into a 25-100% lift
the key is md5 of the composite Dex drafts as the grain, so the two describe the same rows; MetricFlow needs a single-column primary entity

declarations.description: One row per study year: the Day-Off Index and each source's lift.

population.rule: Study years with at least one index component.

day_off_index.null_rule: NULL until every component source has a lift

assumptions.chosen: geometric mean within each source, then across sources, equal weights
assumptions.detail: lifts are ratios; the geometric mean keeps one noisy source from dominating
ln(0) is undefined; a component that fell to zero still pulls the index down hard

assumptions.chosen: NULL until every component source has a lift
